papers.title: N-Polar AlGaN/GaN Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor
papers.summary: Heterojunction bipolar transistors based on the III-Nitride systems have significantly lower performance than field effect transistors due to challenges associated with p-type doping of the base. N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBTs can overcome these challenges by polarization-induced holes in the base and base-emitter interface. We experimentally demonstrate the first N-polar AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy on GaN substrate without emitter regrowth. The HBTs exhibit a peak current gain of approximately 15, peak differential current gain of approximately 18, and emitter-area-normalized peak current densities exceeding 20 kA/cm^2 and 66 kA/cm^2 for emitter areas of 10 x 10 um^2 and 3 x 10 um^2, respectively. The specific contact resistance for base is estimated 1.32 x 10^{-2} Ohm.cm^2. The open-base breakdown voltage is characterized ~63 V for a 300 nm collector without dielectric passivation. This work lays the foundation for future development of N-polar III-Nitride HBTs for next-generation RF applications.

papers.title: WSe <sub>2</sub> p-MOSFETs With Nb-Doped WS <sub>2</sub> Contacts Deposited Using Atomic Layer Deposition
papers.summary: WSe 2 p-MOSFETs with Nb-doped WS 2 contacts formed using atomic layer deposition are demonstrated. The devices are fabricated using a technique that aligns the contact metallization with the Nb-doped WS 2 contacts using a selective oxidation process. Devices with source/drain spacing of $0.11~\mu $ m have on-state current of $98.6~\mu $ A/ $\mu $ m at ${V}_{\text {DS}} = -1$ V at a channel carrier concentration of $\sim ~7.5\times 10^{{12}}$ cm ${}^{-{2}}$ . The results provide a promising CMOS-compatible pathway to create low-resistance contacts to 2D-channel transistors.

papers.title: 3.0-W/mm Output Power Density at W-Band From Enhancement-Mode AlGaN/GaN HEMT With Free-Standing T-Gate
papers.summary: This letter reports on high-performance enhancement-mode (E-mode) GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) for W-band applications. The E-mode HEMT was realized via a gate-recess etching process, exhibiting a positive threshold voltage ( ${V}_{\text {th}}\text {)}$ of 0.41 V, a peak transconductance ( ${G}_{\text {m}}\text {)}$ of 0.73 S/mm, and a maximum drain current density ( ${I}_{\text {d-{ma}{x}}}\text {)}$ of 1.35 A/mm. To overcome gate-head-induced extrinsic fringing capacitance, the proposed device employed an optimized free-standing T-gate (FT-gate) with a gate stem height ( ${H}_{\text {s}}\text {)}$ of 250 nm and a gate length ( ${L}_{\text {g}}\text {)}$ of 120 nm. Small-signal characterization revealed a peak current-gain cutoff frequency ( ${f}_{\text {T}}\text {)}$ of 117 GHz and a peak maximum oscillation frequency ( ${f}_{\max }\text {)}$ of 275 GHz, yielding an outstanding ${f}_{\text {T}} \times {L}_{\text {g}}$ of 14.04 GHz $\cdot \mu $ m. Load-pull measurements at 92 GHz demonstrated an output power density ( ${P}_{\text {out}}\text {)}$ of 3.0 W/mm at a drain-source voltage ( ${V}_{\text {ds}}\text {)}$ of 12 V. These competitive results establish the proposed technological platform as a promising candidate for next-generation E-mode GaN HEMTs.

papers.title: Impact of Scaling on the Temperature Dependence of GaN HEMTs
papers.summary: We report the temperature-dependent DC and small-signal RF characteristics of GaN high-electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) with aggressively scaled source–drain spacing ( ${L}_{\textit {SD}}\text {)}$ and gate length ( ${L}_{G}\text {)}$ . Devices fabricated using HRL Laboratories’ T3.5 technology exhibit superior temperature-dependent performance with the reduction in ${L}_{\textit {SD}}$ . Devices with ${L}_{\textit {SD}} =150$ nm achieve a maximum drain current ${I}_{\textit {D,max}} = 2.28\pm 0.04$ A/mm, a current gain cutoff frequency ${f}_{T} = 222\pm 14$ GHz, and a maximum oscillation frequency ${f}_{\textit {max}} = 329\pm 10$ GHz. Importantly, these scaled devices exhibit excellent high-temperature performance up to $300~^{\circ }$ C, with ${I}_{\textit {D,max}}$ , small-signal RF gain, and ${f}_{T}$ exhibiting smaller changes with temperature compared to longer ${L}_{\textit {SD}}$ devices. Device simulations confirm experimental observations, indicating that as ${L}_{\textit {SD}}$ is reduced and approaches the electron’s mean-free path, carriers in the channel region undergo predominantly quasi-ballistic transport between the source and drain. Consequently, these devices exhibit reduced temperature dependence. These findings, therefore, provide a unique experimental framework to understand temperature-dependent carrier transport in aggressively scaled GaN HEMTs.

papers.title: N-Polar GaN HEMT Operating at 800 °C in Air for 1 h With Minimum I ON / I OFF = 1900
papers.summary: An N-polar gallium nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) with a p-GaN gate is developed, and its operation at $800~^{\circ }$ C in air is demonstrated. At drain-to-source voltage ( ${V}_{\textit {DS}}\text {)}$ of 2 and 6 V, the device exhibits on-current ( ${I}_{\textit {ON}}\text {)}$ of 46 and 80 mA/mm, respectively, with corresponding on/off current ratio ( ${I}_{\textit {ON}}/{I}_{\textit {OFF}}\text {)}$ of 3400 and 2400. These values represent the highest simultaneous ${I}_{\textit {ON}}$ and ${I}_{\textit {ON}}/{I}_{\textit {OFF}}$ reported for any transistor operating at $800~^{\circ }$ C in air. Furthermore, the HEMT maintains stable operation during a 60 min thermal-stress test at $800~^{\circ }$ C, with minimal degradation in ${I}_{\textit {ON}}$ and ${I}_{\textit {ON}}/{I}_{\textit {OFF}}$ . After 60 min, ${I}_{\textit {ON}}$ remains at 40 and 70 mA/mm at ${V}_{\textit {DS}} =2$ and 6 V, respectively, while the corresponding ${I}_{\textit {ON}}/{I}_{\textit {OFF}}$ ratio remains high at 2500 and 1900. These results highlight the potential of N-polar GaN HEMTs for high-temperature and harsh-environment electronics.

papers.title: 8-in. wafer-scale uniform growth of GaN-on-silicon epilayers for near-eye micro-displays
papers.summary: Heteroepitaxial growth of high-quality gallium nitride (GaN) films and their uniform light-emitting diode (LED) structures on 8-in.-wafer-scale silicon (Si) substrates remains a significant challenge due to large lattice and thermal mismatches for the critical control of threading dislocations (TDs) and wafer bowing. Here, we proposed a novel variable growth rate strategy to grow a 6.7-μm-thick, crack-free GaN layer on an 8-in. Si(111) substrate. By carefully managing the thermal stress and the interactions between TDs during epitaxial growth, we could reduce the TD density to approximately 8.0 × 107 cm−2, thereby implying very high-quality GaN epi-layers on Si substrates compared to previous reports. Moreover, blue LED structures were grown on this GaN template, exhibiting a standard deviation of 1.1 nm in peak wavelength and a wafer bowing of 16 μm over the entire 8-in. wafer. This epi-wafer was finally used to fabricate micro-LED arrays via direct 8-in. wafer bonding, revealing the great potential of GaN-on-Si techniques for near-eye micro-displays.

papers.title: Demonstration of Nitrogen-Polar GaN HEMTs With ALD Regrown n <sup>+</sup> Contacts
papers.summary: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is a versatile growth technique for producing high-quality, uniform, and conformal films with precise thickness control at low substrate temperatures. N-polar GaN HEMTs incorporating ALD-regrown n + GaN layers for source/drain contacts in high-performance RF power application are demonstrated. Ohmic contacts were realized without the need for alloyed contacts or high-temperature MBE/MOCVD-regrown n + contacts during device fabrication. A low metal-to-2DEG contact resistance of $0.36~\Omega \cdot $ mm was achieved, falling within the lower end of the range typically reported for Ti/Al/Ni/Au alloyed contacts. N-polar GaN Schottky-gate HEMTs fabricated utilizing the ALD-regrown n + layer demonstrated excellent DC and RF performance at ${L}_{\text {G}} =370$ nm, reaching a drain current above 1 A/mm, a peak gate transconductance of 590 mS/mm, an on resistance of $1.2~\Omega \cdot $ mm, and a pad de-embedded ${f}_{\text {MAX}}$ exceeding 108 GHz. Moreover, at 10 GHz, the device delivered an output power of 4 W/mm with an associated power added efficiency of 55.9% at ${V}_{\text {DS,Q}} =18$ V. Additionally, the output power increased further to 4.7 W/mm at ${V}_{\text {DS,Q}} =20$ V. These results highlight the feasibility of ALD-regrown n + layers for realizing low-resistance ohmic contacts in GaN HEMTs, while reducing fabrication cost and complexity.

papers.title: Self-Assembled Triangular Sc-rich Nanodomains: The Orign of Anomalous Alloy Scattering in ScAlN/GaN Heterostructures
papers.summary: Wurtzite scandium aluminium nitride (ScAlN) alloys hold substantial potential for GaN heterostructure high-electron mobility transistors, owing to their large spontaneous polarization gradient and the ability to achieve precise lattice matching at heterointerface. Nevertheless, despite continuous advances in epitaxy and device fabrication, the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) mobility in ScAlN/GaN heterostructures remains persistently limited, and the underlying microscopic origin remains elusive. Here, we uncover an anomalous electron scattering mechanism from laterally correlated alloy disorder that spontaneously develops within the ScAlN barrier driven by strain-field undulations imposed by threading dislocations. Dislocation strain field partitions the growth front into nanoscale domains with distinct strain states, driving anisotropic diffusion of Sc adatoms and yielding crystallographically oriented triangular Sc-rich nanodomains. Reducing the threading dislocation density from 2.8E10 to 4.4E8 cm^-2 suppresses areal density of nanodomains by more than two orders of magnitude. As a result, low-temperature Hall mobility increases from 1800 to 11995 cm^2*V^-1*s^-1. These findings establish dislocation-mediated Sc-rich nanodomains as the dominant source of anomalously strong alloy scattering, resolving the mobility bottleneck for high-performance nitride electronics.
